source_review.notes: Reviewed Bloom's original paper; primary Kirsch-Mitzenmacher double-hashing, Putze-Sanders-Singler cache-efficient, Bose et al. finite false-positive, Broder-Mitzenmacher survey, and Naor-Yogev adversarial papers; plus the NIST false-positive-analysis record. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Mathematical and systems claims remain scoped to each paper's model and the chapter's explicit assumptions.

evidence: Checked universe U, represented set S, distinct cardinality n, bit count m, probes k, bits/item b, occupied count J, occupancy rho, position multiset P(x), and absent-query domain U\S.
Checked exact per-bit zero probability, exponential approximation, approximate false-positive expression, empirical X/q, and confidence bounds remain distinct quantities.
Checked maybe/definitely-absent, false positive, and forbidden ordinary-filter false negative use the one-sided-error contract consistently.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter labels the familiar exponential expression as a standard approximation rather than an exact finite probability.

evidence: Recomputed m=10000,n=1000,k=7 approximation as 0.008193722 and real optimum k=6.93147.
Recomputed n=5000,p=0.01 sizing as 47925.2919 bits, 9.58506 bits/item, and real k=6.64386.
Recomputed finite model k=4 occupancy 52 bits and 281/10000=0.0281 false positives; approximation minimum occurs at k=6 and finite-query minimum at k=4.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The model's empirical minimum is specific to one construction set, mixer, layout, and query range; it is not evidence against the asymptotic optimum.

evidence: Re-derived per-bit zero probability (1-1/m)^(kn), its exp(-kn/m) limit, and the additional mean-occupancy substitution behind the standard query approximation.
Re-derived approximate optimum k=(m/n)ln2 and target sizing m=-n ln(p)/(ln2)^2.
Verified compatible monotone insertion establishes no false negatives without any random-hash independence premise.
Verified compatible bitwise OR preserves union membership, whereas AND does not reproduce a freshly built exact intersection filter.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Exact finite occupancy conditioning and adaptive guarantees are discussed but not fully derived or mechanically proved.

evidence: Reviewed n=0, m/k zero, empty/all-one filters, duplicate insertions, overload, repeated positions, modulo bias, zero/short steps, integer overflow, tail bits, and allocation/length bounds.
Reviewed deletion/shared bits, hash/seed/canonical-byte drift, corrupt/truncated encoding, rolling compatibility, partial concurrent publication, snapshots, union/intersection, and rebuild.

Reviewed structured/low-entropy keys, public chosen-query search and replay, keyed rotation, rate limits, multiple seeds/distributions, confidence intervals, cache locality, and downstream cost reversal.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes serialization, concurrency, deletion, corruption, security, cache, SIMD, I/O, workload sampling, and production integration.

evidence: The model builds each filter solely through monotone integer bitwise OR and queries with the identical visible position function.
It exhaustively verifies all sixteen members are positive for k=4 and that an all-zero filter rejects members plus ten absent values.
It evaluates k=1 through 8 over the same 10000 absent integers and exact output checks sizing, winners, occupancy, false-positive count/rate, and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: The fixed-width mixer is educational and unkeyed; neither universality, independence, cryptographic security, nor Python integer portability is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed no-false-negative proof from fixed canonical policy and complete insertion through monotonicity, publication, preservation, and identical query positions.
Reviewed sizing derivation from ideal probe assumptions through approximation, real optimization, integer/alignment choices, cardinality headroom, and finite/empirical comparison.
Reviewed evidence proof from pinned implementation/generators through exact-set oracle, member exhaustiveness, intervals, distributions, adversarial search, and compatibility/failure gates.
proof_review.notes: These proofs do not establish a concrete serialized library, concurrent memory model, finite exact probability, or adaptively secure filter.

evidence: Deterministic membership, approximate sizing, and empirical-evidence arguments are separately labeled.
Independent uniform probes, absent-query distribution, finite layout, double-hash correlation, and integer/cache constraints are explicitly attached to claims.
The finite winner, reference reachability, and successful execution are not generalized into universal optimality or deployment fitness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every security/adaptive statement requires a threat model beyond average fresh-random-query false-positive probability.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent recomputation reproduced all displayed sizing, occupancy, approximation, finite false-positive, confidence, and cost calculations.
All seven final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local Markdown/front-matter/link/snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No randomized repeated-seed experiment, exact finite distribution engine, packed filter, production hash, cache/SIMD benchmark, concurrency/fault test, adversarial deployment, I/O integration, or service-level experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter centers one-sided membership semantics, separates deterministic correctness from probabilistic efficiency, and distinguishes standard approximation, exact finite analysis, realized rate, confidence, and adaptive risk.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed canonical encoding and policy identity, bounds and tail bits, double-hash cycles, cache-aware variants, immutable/concurrent publication, serialization/checksum, overload/rebuild, telemetry, statistical trials, adaptive abuse, and end-to-end saved work.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review states the contract and approximation caveat; the finite k sweep makes model-versus-realization visible; ten examples span derivation, deletion, overload, hashing, composition, statistics, cost, and adversaries; five exercises provide complete matched solutions.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Bloom, Kirsch, Mitzenmacher, Putze, Sanders, Singler, Bose, Christensen, Naor, Yogev, database, security, probability, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither an exact finite probability theorem, universal hash family, cryptographic/adaptive security, packed/serialized/concurrent implementation, production false-positive rate, certification, nor deployment fitness.
